title: ASML: Not Just A Monopoly In EUV Lithography (NASDAQ:ASML)
summary: This article examines ASML's dominant position in the semiconductor lithography market, particularly its 100% share in EUV and 88% share in DUV Immersion. It highlights ASML's market leadership in both unit shipments and revenue for lithography equipment in 2019, showcasing its continued growth in EUV system sales. The author discusses the competition and growth drivers for ASML in key technologies for next-node semiconductor devices.

title: ASML Ships Multi-Beam Inspection Tool for 5 nm
summary: ASML has announced the successful integration and testing of its first-generation HMI multibeam inspection (MBI) system, the eScan1000, designed for 5 nm nodes and beyond. This new tool significantly increases throughput for defect inspection by simultaneously scanning nine beams and is suitable for both physical and voltage contrast inspection in R&D and high-volume manufacturing. The first system has been shipped to a customer for qualification, with future plans for increased beams and resolution.

title: EDGAR Filing Documents for 0000937966-20-000011
summary: This SEC EDGAR filing details the Form 20-F annual report for ASML Holding NV, accession number 0000937966-20-000011, filed on February 12, 2020. It includes numerous documents such as the integrated report, various exhibits, and graphic files related to the company's governance, strategy, and financial performance for the period ending December 31, 2019. The filing provides comprehensive information about ASML's operations and financial status.

title: Trump administration pressed Dutch hard to cancel China chip-equipment sale - sources
summary: The Trump administration engaged in a high-level campaign to pressure the Dutch government into canceling the sale of advanced chip manufacturing technology from ASML to a Chinese customer. This effort, involving Secretary of State Mike Pompeo and a classified intelligence briefing for the Dutch Prime Minister, aimed to prevent China from acquiring technology essential for advanced microprocessors. The pressure appears to have been successful, as the Dutch government did not renew ASML's export license for the machine.

title: IBD Stock Of The Day: ASML Holding Breaks Out To New High
summary: ASML Holding (ASML) broke out to a new high on Thursday from a three-weeks-tight pattern, near a buy point of $252.21. The stock's relative strength line is at a record high, with a Relative Strength rating of 96. This breakout follows previous flat base-on-base and cup-with-handle patterns.

title: Ushio’s Breakthrough In The Niche Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography market
summary: Ushio (TYO:6925) has achieved a breakthrough in the Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) lithography market by perfecting a light source for testing patterned EUV masks, a critical component for enabling next-generation semiconductor manufacturing at nodes lower than 7nm. This innovation fills a crucial gap in the industry, positioning Ushio as a sole supplier for this niche and vital technology. The CEO, Koji Naito, highlighted that testing equipment was a bottleneck for EUV and their solution will boost production efficiency and yields, with the technology expected to turn profitable in the next fiscal year.

title: Unlocks the Next Growth Phase with Semiconductor Manufacturing
summary: This article announces a new report on the global Semiconductor Manufacturing Equipment's Market by Research N Reports. The report forecasts a 6.9% CAGR, reaching US$ 70800 million by 2023, up from US$ 47400 million in 2017. It highlights the market fundamentals, regional market, global economic industry development, and key players in this sector.

title: Lam Research, ASML earnings spark ‘relief rally’ for chip-equipment sector, but doubts remain
summary: Shares of chip-equipment companies like Lam Research Corp. and ASML Holding NV saw a "relief rally" after both companies provided better-than-expected earnings and outlooks. Despite this positive movement, analysts remain concerned about the potential impact of trade-war issues on the sector. Lam Research reiterated its forecast that the September quarter was the trough for equipment sales, while ASML offered an encouraging forecast for 2019.

title: Intel Again Cuts Stake in ASML
summary: Intel has further reduced its stake in lithography vendor ASML to below 3%, following similar reductions by other major chipmakers like Samsung and TSMC. This move comes after an initial $4 billion investment in 2012 by Intel to accelerate extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography development. Despite the stake reduction, ASML's stock price has soared by approximately 350% since Intel's initial investment, with EUV technology now nearing production deployment.

title: 25 Overstuffed Stocks
summary: This article identifies the 25 most overvalued U.S. stocks according to Morningstar's price/fair value tool, emphasizing that while these stocks are expensive, many are good investments at the right price. It details three specific companies—Netflix, Ferrari, and Aetna—highlighting reasons for their high valuations and Morningstar analysts' fair value estimates, suggesting waiting for better entry points. The author clarifies that "overstuffed" refers to their current high price relative to fair value, not a judgment of their inherent quality.

title: Can This Little-Known Chip Company Preserve Moore’s Law?
summary: This article highlights how ASML Holding NV, a lesser-known Dutch company, is crucial for the future of the global semiconductor industry. It explores the challenge of continuing to make chips more powerful while maintaining their compact size, effectively preserving Moore's Law. ASML is positioned as the potential solution to this industry-wide hurdle.

title: Samsung (KRX:005930) Moving Swiftly to Sell Stakes to Raise Abundant Levels of Cash
summary: Samsung is selling stakes in several companies, including Seagate, Rambus, ASML Holding NV, and Sharp, to raise cash. This decision comes after the costly Galaxy Note 7 recall and a general move to shed non-core assets under heir apparent Lee Jae-yong. The funds raised might also be used to expedite the launch of the Galaxy S8 to offset losses.

title: HMI agrees to NT$100m buyout bid from ASML
summary: Hermes Microvision Inc (HMI) accepted a NT$100 billion (US$3.09 billion) buyout offer from ASML Holding NV, aiming to jointly develop advanced inspection technologies for smaller chips and address challenges in sub-10 nanometer dimensions. The acquisition will make HMI a wholly-owned subsidiary of ASML, boost HMI's e-beam business, and enable it to compete better with rivals. The deal marks the second-largest acquisition in Taiwan this year.

title: TSMC Orders EUV Lithography Tools For Production
summary: TSMC has ordered two new EUV lithography machines and plans to upgrade two existing ones from ASML, signaling their intent to implement EUV at the 10nm node by 2016. Despite historical delays, EUV technology has received significant investment, and ASML reports progress in critical areas like source power and throughput, with a goal of achieving 1500 wafers per day by 2016 for critical layers in chip production. This move suggests EUV is finally maturing for high-volume manufacturing, with ASML expecting to ship 50 to 60 EUV systems annually by 2020.

title: Intel and ASML Holdings EUV Lithography Slated for 2016 Debut – End of 10nm Cycle
summary: Intel and ASML Holdings are collaborating on EUV Lithography, with a planned debut in 2016, marking a shift in semiconductor manufacturing past the 10nm node. ASML, the leading supplier of photolithography systems, is expected to provide the necessary technology, though the exact timeline depends on R&D progress. Intel, a major shareholder in ASML, anticipates utilizing this next-generation litho process after its 10nm processors.

title: ASML customers ‘intensify’ EUV development
summary: ASML's customers are intensifying their development efforts in extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography, with CEO Eric Meurice expressing confidence in its capabilities for the 10 nm node. The company's acquisition of Cymer has significantly advanced light source development, enabling routine production at 40 wafers per hour. ASML projects increased wafer per hour throughput and expects higher tool shipments, anticipating significant revenue contribution from EUV tools and overall sales growth, driven by key technology nodes and the mobile DRAM market.

title: ASML chief Meurice steps down
summary: Eric Meurice, CEO of ASML for over eight years, is stepping down in July to become chairman of ASML Holdings, with current CFO Peter Wennink taking over as CEO. The transition comes as ASML nears the completion of its merger with Cymer and continues to make progress in its extreme ultraviolet (EUV) production tools, despite facing some delays. Meurice's tenure saw significant growth in ASML's sales and net profit, and the company expects continued progress in EUV lithography with rising unit shipments in the coming years.

title: Cymer, Inc. (CYMI) Investor Lawsuit to Stop Takeover Announced by Shareholders Foundation
summary: The Shareholders Foundation announced an investor lawsuit challenging the proposed takeover of Cymer, Inc. (CYMI) at approximately $81.64 per share. The lawsuit alleges that the company is being sold too cheaply via an unfair process, highlighting Cymer's recent financial improvements and stock growth. Investors who bought CYMI shares before October 17, 2012, are encouraged to contact the Shareholders Foundation.

title: Dutch Firm to Buy Cymer for $2.55B
summary: Dutch firm ASML Holding NV has agreed to acquire San Diego-based laser maker Cymer Inc. for approximately $2.55 billion in a cash and stock transaction. The acquisition, which sees Cymer transition from a supplier to a subsidiary of its primary customer, aims to accelerate the development of advanced lithography technology for semiconductor manufacturing. Despite the acquisition, Cymer is expected to maintain and potentially grow its operations in San Diego, with its commercial operations managed as an independent division.

title: ASML Acquiring Cymer for $2.5B to Boost Chip Tech | Business | Oct 2012
summary: ASML Holding NV is set to acquire its light source supplier, Cymer Inc., for approximately $2.5 billion in stock, a move intended to accelerate the development of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) semiconductor lithography technology. The deal, which will see Cymer operate as an independent division and a DUV/EUV light source center for ASML, aims to enhance efficiency in EUV technology development and simplify the supply chain. Cymer shareholders will receive $20 in cash and 1.15 ASML shares for each Cymer share.

title: TSMC and ASML Reach Agreement to Develop Next Generation Lithography Technologies as an Extension of Long-Term Partnership
summary: TSMC announced its participation in ASML Holding N.V.'s Customer Co-Investment Program, investing 838 million euros to acquire a 5% equity stake and committing 276 million euros over five years to ASML’s R&D programs. This initiative aims to accelerate the development and industrialization of next-generation semiconductor manufacturing technologies, including extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography and 450-millimeter lithography tools, to control wafer costs and advance Moore's Law. This agreement extends their long-term partnership, building on their successful collaboration in 193-nanometer immersion lithography.
